questions.stem: What is the news report mainly about?
options: A) How college students can handle their psychological problems.
B) Why college students are more likely to have stress problems.
C) Why sufficient sleep is important for college students.
D) How college students can improve their sleep habits.

explain.定位:
You probably think college students are experts at sleeping, but parties, preparations for tests,
personal problems and general stress can wreck a student's sleep habits, which can be bad for
the body and the mind.
你大概觉得大学生最擅长睡觉，但聚会、备考、个人问题和普遍的压力会毁掉学生的睡眠习
惯，而这对身心都有害。
explain.信号:
开头点题 + 转折 but 后是真意。这是新闻第一句，承担点题功能；句中 but 之后才抛出真
正话题——睡眠被毁、有害身心。整篇随后都在围绕"睡眠对大学生有多重要"展开（睡不够
的风险、开设睡眠课、睡比临时备考更管用），证明开头这句就是主旨落点。
explain.替换:
can wreck a student's sleep habits, which can be bad for the body and the mind ↔
Why sufficient sleep is important for college students.
"破坏睡眠有害身心"="充足睡眠很重要"
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音确实念到 psychological problems，A 把它写进选项诱你"听到就选"。但原文只是把
心理问题列为睡眠不足的一个后果，全篇并没在教"怎么处理心理问题"，A 偷换了重心。
借用原文：psychological problems
B) 原词陷阱
录音提到 general stress 是毁睡眠的原因之一，B 借这个词诱选。但 B 说"为何大学生更容
易有压力问题"，原文压根没解释压力的成因，只把压力当作影响睡眠的因素之一，B 把一
个次要因素抬成了主题。
借用原文：general stress
D) 偷换概念
录音反复出现 sleep habits，还提到开设 Improving Your Sleep Habits 的课，D 借此极具
迷惑性。但 D 问的是"怎么改善睡眠习惯"（方法），全篇却是在讲"睡眠为什么重要"（原
因），重心一个落在 how、一个落在 why，D 偷换了问法。
借用原文：Improving Your Sleep Habits

questions.stem: What is the finding of the new study published in the journal Learning and Memory?
options: A) It is not easy to improve one's sleep habits.
B) It is not good for students to play video games.
C) Making last-minute preparations for tests may be less effective than sleeping.
D) Students who are better prepared generally get higher scores in examinations.

explain.定位:
On top of all that, a new study published in the journal Learning and Memory finds you are
probably better off sleeping than making last-minute preparations for a test.
除此之外，一项发表在《学习与记忆》期刊上的新研究发现：比起临时抱佛脚准备考试，你
睡一觉很可能更划算。
explain.信号:
研究信号 a new study ... finds。a new study published in the journal Learning and
Memory finds 是明确的研究结论信号，finds 之后那句就是研究真正的发现。题干问的正
是这项研究的 finding，信号与题干直接对上，定位无误。
explain.替换:
you are probably better off sleeping than making last-minute preparations for a test ↔
Making last-minute preparations for tests may be less effective than sleeping.
"睡觉更划算"="临时备考没睡觉有效"
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音前文提到 sleep habits、还有改善睡眠习惯的课，A 借此诱选。但"改善睡眠习惯不容
易"是 A 自造的说法，那项研究的 finding 与"习惯难不难改"无关，A 答非所问。
借用原文：sleep habits
B) 张冠李戴
录音确实念到 Two hundred college kids were taught to play some unfamiliar video
games，B 借 video games 诱选。但游戏只是这项研究的实验材料，原文从没说"玩游戏不
好"，B 把实验工具误读成了研究结论。
借用原文：Two hundred college kids were taught to play some unfamiliar video games
D) 未提及
Students who are better prepared generally get higher scores in examinations."准备
越充分分越高"是太顺耳的常识，但这项研究恰恰说"睡觉比临时备考更管用"，原文从没
说"准备充分就得高分"，D 是凭常识硬填、未提及。
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 Long queues, delayed flights and overcrowding at airports have become almost as much a topic for
conversation in Britain as the traditional complaining about the weather. Meanwhile there are complaints
that poor service at London's major airports is discouraging foreigners from doing business in Britain.
Much of the criticism is directed at the British Airports Authority, which runs seven major airports,
including the three main ones serving London. The Competition Commission is now to investigate
whether the British Airports Authority needs to sell off some of its assets. The idea is that competition
between rival operators would lead to better service at airports. The British Airports Authority, recently
bought by a Spanish company, says the root cause of the problem is not the ownership structure but a
lack of runway and terminal capacity, which it is addressing through a program of heavy investment.

questions.stem: What is the Competition Commission going to investigate?
options: A) Whether adequate investment is being made to improve airport facilities.
B) Whether the British Airports Authority should sell off some of its assets.
C) Whether the Spanish company could offer better service.
D) Whether more airports should be built around London.

explain.定位:
The Competition Commission is now to investigate whether the British Airports Authority
needs to sell off some of its assets.
竞争委员会现在将调查英国机场管理局是否需要出售其部分资产。
explain.信号:
题干主语原样复现处即落点。录音里出现 The Competition Commission is now to
investigate 这一短语，与题干主语 the Competition Commission 对应，investigate 后
面紧跟的 whether 从句就是 “要调查的内容”，这就是答案句的定位信号。
explain.替换:
whether the British Airports Authority needs to sell off some of its assets ↔
Whether the British Airports Authority should sell off some of its assets.
needs to ≈ should，其余近乎原句
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
adequate investment 借了录音结尾 a program of heavy investment 的 investment 一
词制造耳熟，但那是英国机场管理局自述的应对措施，根本不是竞争委员会 “要调查” 的事，
答非所问。
借用原文：a program of heavy investment
C) 张冠李戴
the Spanish company 取自录音 recently bought by a Spanish company，西班牙公司
确实被念到，但录音只是交代管理局新东家，竞争委员会要查的是 “是否该卖资产”，不是
“西班牙公司能否提供更好服务”，张冠李戴。
借用原文：recently bought by a Spanish company
D) 未提及
录音提到 the three main ones serving London，伦敦确被念到，但全篇没有任何 “应再多
建机场” 的意思，more airports should be built around London 属凭 London 一词臆
造，未提及。
借用原文：the three main ones serving London

questions.stem: What is the root cause of the poor service at British airports according to the British Airports Authority?
options: C) Lack of innovation and competition.
D) Lack of runway and terminal capacity.

explain.定位:
The British Airports Authority... says the root cause of the problem is not the ownership
structure but a lack of runway and terminal capacity, which it is addressing through a program
of heavy investment.
英国机场管理局……表示，问题的根本原因不是产权结构，而是跑道和航站楼容量不足，它
正通过一项大规模投资计划来解决这一问题。
explain.信号:
not…but… 转折后才是真原因。答案句用 the root cause of the problem is not the
ownership structure but a lack of runway and terminal capacity 的 not…but… 结构：
not 后是被否定的假原因，but 后才是管理局认定的真原因——but 之后才是落点。
explain.替换:
a lack of runway and terminal capacity ↔ Lack of runway and terminal capacity.
近乎原词照搬，仅去冠词
explain.排除:
A) 与原文相反
Poor ownership structure. 直接搬录音 not the ownership structure 的原词，极易 “听到
就选”，可它恰恰是管理局明确否定的那个假原因——not 后的内容正话反说，与原文相
反。
借用原文：not the ownership structure
B) 未提及
Inefficient management. 听感上像在批评机场，但录音从头到尾没说过管理低效，它只在
产权与跑道容量之间二选一，management 一词未现，属未提及。
C) 张冠李戴
Lack of innovation and competition. 里的 competition 容易让人联想到录音里的
competition between rival operators，但那是竞争委员会设想的 “解决办法” 而非管理局
认定的 “根本原因”，把手段当成因，张冠李戴。
借用原文：competition between rival operators would lead to better service

questions.stem: What do tobacco companies have to do under the law in Massachusetts?
options: A) Study the effects of nicotine on young smokers.
B) Set a limit to the production of their cigarettes.
C) Take steps to reduce nicotine in their products.
D) Report the nicotine content of their cigarettes.

explain.定位:
Under the law in Massachusetts, tobacco companies have to measure the nicotine content of
every type of cigarette and report the results.
根据马萨诸塞州的法律，烟草公司必须测量每一种香烟的尼古丁含量，并上报结果。
explain.信号:
义务信号 have to 后接动词。Under the law in Massachusetts, tobacco companies
have to measure…and report the results 里 have to（必须）是义务信号词，它后面接的
两个动词 measure 与 report 就是法律要求做的事，这句正是答案句。
explain.替换:
measure the nicotine content of every type of cigarette and report the results ↔
Report the nicotine content of their cigarettes
report the results=Report the nicotine content
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
选项 Study the effects of nicotine on young smokers 借了原文反复出现的 nicotine 和
young smokers 来诱选，但"研究尼古丁对年轻烟民的影响"是波士顿公共卫生部门做的
事，不是法律要求烟草公司做的，属答非所问。
借用原文：The biggest increases tended to be in brands that were popular with young smokers
B) 未提及
Set a limit to the production of their cigarettes（限制香烟产量）在录音里完全没出现，
法律只要求"测量并上报含量"，没有任何关于限产的表述，属无中生有。
C) 偷换概念
Take steps to reduce nicotine in their products 用了话题核心词 reduce nicotine 来诱
选，但法律要求的是 measure（测量）与 report（上报），不是"降低"含量；录音后文恰
恰说含量在上涨，公司并未被要求降含量，属偷换概念。
借用原文：measure the nicotine content of every type of cigarette and report the results

questions.stem: What do we learn from the study by the Department of Public Health in Boston?
options: A) The biggest increase in nicotine content tended to be in brands young smokers like.
B) Brands which contain higher nicotine content were found to be much more popular.
C) Tobacco companies refused to discuss the detailed nicotine content of their products.
D) Big tobacco companies were frank with their customers about the hazards of smoking.

explain.定位:
Ninety-two were found to have higher nicotine yields than they did six years previously. The
biggest increases tended to be in brands that were popular with young smokers.
其中九十二种被发现尼古丁释放量比六年前更高。涨幅最大的往往出现在受年轻烟民欢迎的
牌子上。
explain.信号:
最高级 the biggest increases 点核心发现。The biggest increases tended to be in
brands that were popular with young smokers 用最高级 the biggest 标出调查最突出
的发现，最高级处往往就是出题点，这句即答案句。
explain.替换:
The biggest increases tended to be in brands that were popular with young smokers ↔
The biggest increase in nicotine content tended to be in brands young smokers like
popular with young smokers=brands young smokers like
explain.排除:
B) 偷换概念
Brands which contain higher nicotine content were found to be much more popular
盗用原文 higher nicotine、popular 等词，却把逻辑反过来说成"含量高的牌子更受欢
迎"。原文说的是"年轻人爱抽的牌子涨幅最大"，并没说"含量高所以更受欢迎"，因果与主语
都被偷换。
借用原文：The biggest increases tended to be in brands that were popular with young smokers
C) 答非所问
Tobacco companies refused to discuss the detailed nicotine content 借用了原文结尾
discuss the detailed nicotine content of their products 的原话，但"公司拒绝置评"是报
道末尾对公司反应的描述，不是"这项调查的发现"，张冠李戴答非所问。
借用原文：none of them were prepared to comment on this study or discuss the detailed nicotine
content of their products
D) 原词陷阱
Big tobacco companies were frank with their customers about the hazards of
smoking 直接搬了原文 frank with their customers about the dangers of smoking 的措
辞，极易诱选；但这是"公司一向声称"的立场，且也不是"调查发现"的内容，答非所问。
借用原文：The big tobacco companies have always insisted that they are frank with their
customers about the dangers of smoking

questions.stem: What do we learn from the news report about the big tobacco companies?
options: A) They will pay more attention to the quality of their products.
B) They were not prepared to comment on the cigarette study.
C) They promised to reduce the nicotine content in cigarettes.
D) They have not fully realized the harmful effect of nicotine.

explain.定位:
However, none of them were prepared to comment on this study or discuss the detailed
nicotine content of their products.
然而，它们没有一家愿意就这项调查发表评论，也不愿讨论其产品的具体尼古丁含量。
explain.信号:
转折 However 后才是真意。However, none of them were prepared to comment on
this study 由转折词 However 引出，前半句讲公司"一向声称坦诚"是铺垫，转折之后才是
报道要点——它们其实拒绝置评，这句是答案句。
explain.替换:
none of them were prepared to comment on this study ↔
They were not prepared to comment on the cigarette study
none of them=They…not（双重否定转单否定）
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
They will pay more attention to the quality of their products 在录音里没有任何依据，
公司既未承诺也未表示要重视质量，属凭空添加。
C) 与原文相反
They promised to reduce the nicotine content in cigarettes 借了话题核心词 reduce
nicotine content 诱选，但原文恰恰说含量在上涨、且公司连置评都拒绝，根本没承诺降含
量，与原文相反。
借用原文：none of them were prepared to comment on this study or discuss the detailed nicotine
content of their products
D) 与原文相反
They have not fully realized the harmful effect of nicotine 借用原文反复出现的
nicotine 与 dangers of smoking 来诱选，但原文说公司"一向声称对顾客坦诚危害"，恰恰
是"已意识到并声称告知"，并非"没充分意识到危害"，属与原文相反。
借用原文：they are frank with their customers about the dangers of smoking and provide them
with enough detail to make an informed decision

questions.stem: Where does the woman live right now?

explain.定位:
right now, I do live in Holland, but I really don't socialize much with Dutch people
现在呢，我确实住在荷兰，但我跟荷兰人社交其实不多。
explain.信号:
被问者直接应答 + right now 强调。男方问当前住地，女方在 right now, I do live in
Holland 里用 right now 与加重的 do live 直接应答，这种「被问者的直接回答 + 强调
词」就是答案信号，落点在回答方。
explain.替换:
I do live in Holland ↔ Holland.
地名原词直接对应
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
录音里男方提到女方 teaching in Indonesia，Indonesia 是她「教过书」的地方，不是
「现在住的地方」；选项把这个真出现过的国名搬来答 where she lives now，属典型答非
所问。
借用原文：teaching in Indonesia
C) 未提及
录音从头到尾没把 England 作为女方的居住地提及，选项纯属用一个常见英语国家来凑
「学英语」的联想，原文无据。
D) 原词陷阱
Sweden 在录音里是 In Sweden, they have a really cool system called Study Circles 提
到的「某制度所在国」，与女方当前住地无关；选项搬这个真国名来答 where she lives，
是答非所问。
借用原文：In Sweden, they have a really cool system called Study Circles

questions.stem: What does the woman say is the real challenge?
options: A) Talking with her boyfriend in Dutch.
B) Getting a coach who can offer real help.
C) Acquiring the necessary ability to socialize.
D) Learning a language where it is not spoken.

explain.定位:
So I think that's really the challenge for people who live in a country where their target
language isn't spoken.
所以我觉得，对于住在目标语言没人说的国家里的人来说，这才是真正的难处。
explain.信号:
强调词 the challenge 收束句。女方用 that's really the challenge for people who live
in a country where their target language isn't spoken 把前面铺垫收成一句结论，really
the challenge 是明确的强调信号，问 the real challenge 就锁这句。
explain.替换:
people who live in a country where their target language isn't spoken ↔
Learning a language where it is not spoken.
从句改写成动名词概括
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音提到女方 I do live in Holland，但荷兰只是她的居住地，不是她说的「真正难处」；选
项把这个真地名搬来答 challenge，答非所问。
借用原文：I do live in Holland
B) 原词陷阱
录音里 a course leader who is there, sort of as a coach and guide 的 coach 是介绍瑞
典 Study Circles 时说的好处，不是女方所说的难处；选项把它包装成「难在找不到好教
练」，与原文定调相反。
借用原文：a course leader who is there, sort of as a coach and guide
C) 偷换概念
录音说的是「没有真实环境去练说」，难点在环境，不在「掌握社交能力」；女方 I really
don't socialize much with Dutch people 只是描述现状，选项却把 socialize 拔高成「要
获得社交能力」，偷换了概念。
借用原文：I really don't socialize much with Dutch people

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest doing to learn to speak a foreign language?
options: A) Practicing reading aloud as often as possible.
B) Listening to language programs on the radio.
C) Trying to speak it as much as one can.
D) Making friends with native speakers.

explain.定位:
But for speaking, there really is no substitute for trying to speak and use the language in a
relaxed atmosphere.
但说到口语，真的没有什么能替代在轻松氛围里去尝试开口、去用这门语言。
explain.信号:
转折 But + 建议结构 no substitute for。前文先把听、读铺一遍，女方用 But for
speaking, there really is no substitute for trying to speak 转折并限定 for speaking，
no substitute for 是「没什么比这更好」的建议信号，转折后才是落点。
explain.替换:
no substitute for trying to speak and use the language ↔ Trying to speak it as much as one can.
「无可替代」=「尽可能多做」
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音提到 reading，但只说有大量东西可读可听，从未建议「朗读 read aloud」来练口
语；选项借 reading 这个原词造出一个原文没有的具体做法。
借用原文：reading
B) 原词陷阱
录音说 There is as much listening exposure as I want，听力输入随手可得，但那是讲
「听、读不缺」，恰恰反衬「练说才难」；选项把 listening 搬来当练口语的建议，答非所
问。
借用原文：There is as much listening exposure as I want
D) 未提及
录音提到 in a relaxed atmosphere、find a club，但没有把「结交母语者朋友」作为练口
语的建议提出；选项用一个看似合理的方法填空，原文无据。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about the Study Circles in Sweden?
options: A) It provides opportunities for language practice.
B) It trains young people's leadership abilities.
C) It offers various courses with credit points.
D) It creates an environment for socializing.

explain.定位:
In Sweden, they have a really cool system called Study Circles; well, it's not… it's like a
course. But really, you just have a course leader who is there, sort of as a coach and guide and
to help out, and you don't get grades, and you go just because you want to learn.
在瑞典，他们有个很棒的制度叫「学习圈」；嗯，它不是……它有点像一门课。但其实呢，
你只是有一个课程引导者在那儿，相当于教练和向导，帮你一把，你不会拿到分数，你来纯
粹是因为你想学。
explain.信号:
专名 Study Circles 后的整段介绍。女方在 a really cool system called Study Circles 之
后整段描述它的样子，这段就是答案句区；信号是「点名某物 + 随即解释它怎么运作」，要
把这几句合起来判它到底提供什么。
explain.替换:
you go just because you want to learn ↔ It provides opportunities for language practice.
「为学而来的轻松学习场」=「提供练习机会」
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
录音里 leader 只出现在 a course leader who is there，指「课程引导者」这个人，根本没
说培养「年轻人的领导力」；选项把 leader 这个词偷换成 leadership 来造一个原文没有的
功能。
借用原文：a course leader who is there
C) 与原文相反
录音明确说 you don't get grades——不打分、没学分，选项 It offers various courses
with credit points. 却说「提供带学分的课程」，与原文恰好相反；it's like a course 只是
说「像门课」，被选项坐实成「有学分的课程」。
借用原文：it's like a course. But really, you just have a course leader who is there, sort of as a
coach and guide and to help out, and you don't get grades

questions.stem: According to an ancient Greek philosopher, it is impossible for us to understand every aspect of our life.
questions.passage:
Ancient Greek Wisdom Inspires Guidelines to Good Life

A) Is it possible to enjoy a peaceful life in a world that is increasingly challenged by threats and uncertainties from wars, terrorism, economic crises and a widespread outbreak of infectious diseases? The answer is yes, according to a new book The 10 Golden Rules: Ancient Wisdom from the Greek Philosophers on Living a Good Life. The book is co-authored by Long Island University's philosophy professor Michael Soupios and economics professor Panos Mourdoukoutas.

B) The wisdom of the ancient Greek philosophers is timeless, says Soupios. The philosophy professor says it is as relevant today as when it was first written many centuries ago. "There is no expiration(失效) date on wisdom." he says. "There is no shelf life on intelligence. I think that things have become very gloomy these days, lots of misunderstanding, misleading cues, a lot of what the ancients would have called sophistry(诡辩). The nice thing about ancient philosophy as offered by the Greeks is that they tended to see life clear and whole, in a way that we tend not to see life today."

C) Soupios, along with his co-author Panos Mourdoukoutas, developed their 10 golden rules by turning to the men behind that philosophy—Aristotle, Socrates, Epictetus and Pythagoras, among others. The first rule—examine your life—is the common thread that runs through the entire book. Soupios says that it is based on Plato's observation that the unexamined life is not worth living. "The Greeks are always concerned about boxing themselves in, in terms of convictions(信念)," he says. Ancient Greek Wisdom Inspires Guidelines to Good Life

A) Is it possible to enjoy a peaceful life in a world that is increasingly challenged by threats and uncertainties from wars, terrorism, economic crises and a widespread outbreak of infectious diseases? The answer is yes, according to a new book The 10 Golden Rules: Ancient Wisdom from the Greek Philosophers on Living a Good Life. The book is co-authored by Long Island University's philosophy professor Michael Soupios and economics professor Panos Mourdoukoutas.

B) The wisdom of the ancient Greek philosophers is timeless, says Soupios. The philosophy professor says it is as relevant today as when it was first written many centuries ago. "There is no expiration(失效) date on wisdom." he says. "There is no shelf life on intelligence. I think that things have become very gloomy these days, lots of misunderstanding, misleading cues, a lot of what the ancients would have called sophistry(诡辩). The nice thing about ancient philosophy as offered by the Greeks is that they tended to see life clear and whole, in a way that we tend not to see life today."

C) Soupios, along with his co-author Panos Mourdoukoutas, developed their 10 golden rules by turning to the men behind that philosophy—Aristotle, Socrates, Epictetus and Pythagoras, among others. The first rule—examine your life—is the common thread that runs through the entire book. Soupios says that it is based on Plato's observation that the unexamined life is not worth living. "The Greeks are always concerned about boxing themselves in, in terms of convictions(信念)," he says. "So take a step back, switch off the automatic pilot and actually stop and reflect about things like our priorities, our values, and our relationships."

D) As we begin to examine our life, Soupios says, we come to Rule No. 2: Worry only about things that you can control. "The individual who promoted this idea was a Stoic philosopher. His name is Epictetus," he says. "And what the Stoics say in general is simply this: There is a larger plan in life. You are not really going to be able to understand all of the dimensions of this plan. You are not going to be able to control the dimensions of this plan."

E) So, Soupios explains, it is not worth it to waste our physical, intellectual and spiritual energy worrying about things that are beyond our control. "I can not control whether or not I wind up getting the disease swine flu, for example," he says. "I mean, there are some cautious steps I can take, but ultimately I can not guarantee myself that. So what Epictetus would say is sitting at home worrying about that would be wrong and wasteful and irrational. You should live your life attempting to identify and control those things which you can genuinely control."

F) To have a meaningful, happy life we need friends. But according to Aristotle—a student of Plato and teacher of Alexander the Great—most relationships don't qualify as true friendships. "Just because I have a business relationship with an individual and I can profit from that relationship, it does not necessarily mean that this person is my friend," Soupios says. "Real friendship is when two individuals share the same soul. It is a beautiful and uncharacteristically poetic image that Aristotle offers."

G) In our pursuit of the good life, he says, it is important to seek out true pleasures—advice which was originally offered by Epicurus. But unlike the modern definition of Epicureanism as a life of indulgence(放纵) and luxury, for the ancient Greeks, it meant finding a state of calm, peace and mental ease.

H) "This was the highest and most desirable form of pleasure and happiness for the ancient Epicureans," Soupios says. "This is something that is very much well worth considering here in the modern era. I do not think that we spend nearly enough time trying to concentrate on achieving a sort of calmness, a sort of contentment in a mental and spiritual way, which was identified by these people as the highest form of happiness and pleasure."

I) Other golden rules counsel us to master ourselves, to avoid excess and not to be a prosperous(发迹的) fool. There are also rules dealing with interpersonal relationships: Be a responsible human being and do not do evil things to others.

J) "This is Hesiod, of course, a younger contemporary poet, we believe, with Homer," Soupios says. "Hesiod offers an idea—which you very often find in some of the world's great religions, in the Judeo-Christian tradition and in Islam and others—that in some sense, when you hurt another human being, you hurt yourself. That damaging other people in your community and in your life, trashing relationships, results in a kind of self-inflicted(自己招致的) spiritual wound."

K) Instead, Soupios says, ancient wisdom urges us to do good. Golden Rule No. 10 for a good life is that kindness toward others tends to be rewarded.

L) "This is Aesop, the fabulist(寓言家), the man of these charming little tales, often told in terms of animals and animal relationships," he says. "I think what Aesop was suggesting is that when you offer a good turn to another human being, one can hope that that good deed will come back and sort of pay a profit to you, the doer of the good deed. Even if there is no concrete benefit paid in response to your good deed, at the very least, the doer of the good deed has the opportunity to enjoy a kind of spiritually enlightened moment."

M) Soupios says following the 10 Golden Rules based on ancient wisdom can guide us to the path of the good life where we stop living as onlookers and become engaged and happier human beings. And that, he notes, is a life worth living.

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about people in pre-industrial Europe?
options: A) They had to work from early morning till late at night.
B) They were so busy working that they only ate simple meals.
C) Their daily routine followed the rhythm of the natural cycle.
D) Their life was much more comfortable than that of today.
questions.passage:
In agrarian(农业的), pre-industrial Europe, "you'd want to wake up early, start working with the sunrise, have a break to have the largest meal, and then you'd go back to work," says Ken Albala, a professor of history at the University of the Pacific. "Later, at 5 or 6, you'd have a smaller supper."

This comfortable cycle, in which the rhythms of the day helped shape the rhythms of the meals, gave rise to the custom of the large midday meal, eaten with the extended family. "Meals are the foundation of the family," says Carole Counihan, a professor at Millersville University in Pennsylvania, "so there was a very important interconnection between eating together" and strengthening family ties.

Since industrialization, maintaining such a slow cultural metabolism has been much harder, with the long midday meal shrinking to whatever could be stuffed into a lunch bucket or bought at a food stand. Certainly, there were benefits. Modern techniques for producing and shipping food led to greater variety and quantity, including a tremendous increase in the amount of animal protein and dairy products available, making us more vigorous than our ancestors.

Yet plenty has been lost too, even in cultures that still live to eat. Take Italy. It's no secret that the Mediterranean diet is healthy, but it was also a joy to prepare and eat. Italians, says Counihan, traditionally began the day with a small meal. The big meal came at around 1 p.m. In between the midday meal and a late, smaller dinner came a small snack. Today, when time zones have less and less meaning, there is little tolerance for offices' closing for lunch, and worsening traffic in cities means workers can't make it home and back fast enough anyway. So the formerly small supper after sundown becomes the big meal of the day, the only one at which the family has a chance to get together. "The evening meal carries the full burden that used to be spread over two meals," says Counihan.

questions.stem: What does "cultural metabolism"(Line l, Para. 3) refer to?
questions.passage:
In agrarian(农业的), pre-industrial Europe, "you'd want to wake up early, start working with the sunrise, have a break to have the largest meal, and then you'd go back to work," says Ken Albala, a professor of history at the University of the Pacific. "Later, at 5 or 6, you'd have a smaller supper."

This comfortable cycle, in which the rhythms of the day helped shape the rhythms of the meals, gave rise to the custom of the large midday meal, eaten with the extended family. "Meals are the foundation of the family," says Carole Counihan, a professor at Millersville University in Pennsylvania, "so there was a very important interconnection between eating together" and strengthening family ties.

Since industrialization, maintaining such a slow cultural metabolism has been much harder, with the long midday meal shrinking to whatever could be stuffed into a lunch bucket or bought at a food stand. Certainly, there were benefits. Modern techniques for producing and shipping food led to greater variety and quantity, including a tremendous increase in the amount of animal protein and dairy products available, making us more vigorous than our ancestors.

Yet plenty has been lost too, even in cultures that still live to eat. Take Italy. It's no secret that the Mediterranean diet is healthy, but it was also a joy to prepare and eat. Italians, says Counihan, traditionally began the day with a small meal. The big meal came at around 1 p.m. In between the midday meal and a late, smaller dinner came a small snack. Today, when time zones have less and less meaning, there is little tolerance for offices' closing for lunch, and worsening traffic in cities means workers can't make it home and back fast enough anyway. So the formerly small supper after sundown becomes the big meal of the day, the only one at which the family has a chance to get together. "The evening meal carries the full burden that used to be spread over two meals," says Counihan.
